questions.question: A dealer marked the price of an item 50% above the cost price. He allowed three successive discounts of 10%, 15% and 20% to a particular customer. As a result, he incurred a loss of ₹410. At what price (in ₹) did he sell the item to the customer?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The MP is 50% above the CP

After three successive discounts of 10%, 15% and 20% loss is Rs. 410.

**Concept:**

If there are three successive discounts of a%, b% and c% on MP

⇒ SP = MP × ((100 - a))/(100)×((100 - b))/(100)× ((100 - c))/(100)

**Formula used:**

Loss = CP - SP

**Calculation:**

Let CP be 100x

⇒ MP = 150x

After three successive discounts of 10%, 15% and 20% on MP

SP = 150x × (90/100) × (85/100) × (80/100)

⇒ 150x × (9/10) × (17/20) × (4\5) = 459x/5

∴ SP = 459x/5

Also loss = 410

⇒ 100x - 459x/5 = 410

⇒ 41x/5 = 410

⇒ x = 50

⇒ SP = (459 × 50)/5 = Rs. 4590 

**Hence SP is 4590.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows 28% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 30%. If he gains ₹30.90 on the sale of one article, then what is the marked price (to the nearest ₹) of the article?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Discount = 28%

Profit = 30%

Profit = ₹ 30.90

**Formula used:**

S.P. = [(100 - Discount%)/100] × M.P.

C.P. = S.P. × [100/(100 + Profit%)]

C.P. = Cost price; M.P. = Marked price; and S.P. = Selling price

**Calculation:**

Let, M.P. = x

S.P. = [(100 - 28)/100] × x = 36x/50

So, C.P. = (36x/50) × [100/(100 + 30)] = (36x/50) × (100/130) = 36x/65

Then, (36x/50) - (36x/65) = 30.90

⇒ 540x/(50 × 65) = 30.90

⇒ x = (30.90 × 50 × 65)/540 = 185.972... ≈ ₹186 (to the nearest ₹)

**∴ The marked price (to the nearest ₹) of the article is ₹186**

questions.question: The marked price of a watch is Rs. 700. A shopkeeper gives two successive discounts and sells the watch at Rs. 315. If the first discount is 10%, then the second discount will be:
questions.solution:
**Given: **

The marked price of the watch is Rs. 700

The selling price of a watch is Rs. 315

1st discount is 10%

**Calculation:**

Let the second discount be x %, then

700 × (100 - 10)% = 700 × 90%

⇒ 630

Now, 630 × (100 - x)% = 315

⇒ (100 - x)/100 = 315/630

⇒ (100 - x)/100 = 1/2

⇒ (100 - x) = 1/2 × 100

⇒ (100 - x) = 50

⇒ x = 50%

**Hence, the 2nd discount is 50%.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

[(100 - 10)/100 × (100 - x)/100] × 700 = 315

9/10 × (100 - x) = 315/7

9/10 × (100 - x) = 45

(100 - x) = 50

x = 50%

**Hence, the correct answer is 50%.**

questions.question: A shopkeeper marked his goods in at 25% higher price than their cost price. Finally, he sold the goods at 30% discount on the marked price. His profit/loss percentage is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

MP is 25% higher than CP

Discount = 30%

**Formula used:**

SP = MP × (100 - L%)/100

L% = L × 100/CP

**Calculation:**

Let CP be Rs. 100x

MP = 125x

SP = 125x × (100 - 30)/100 = 125x × 7/10

SP = 87.5x

Loss = 100x - 87.5x = 12.5x

Loss% = 12.5x × 100/100x = 12.5

**Hence, the required loss is 12.5%**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__** As MP is 25% above CP 

CP : MP = 100 : 125

CP : MP = 4 : 5 ------- (1)

Also CP : MP = (100 - D%) : (100 - P)

CP : MP = 70 : (100 - P) ------- (2)

⇒ 4 : 5 = 70 : (100 - P) -- From (1) and (2)

⇒ 4(100 - P) = 350

⇒ 4P = - 50

P = - 12.5

Profit is negative because there is a loss of 12.5%

**∴ T**he required loss is 12.5%
